Android doesn’t let an app ask for these rights itself — you turn them on once by hand. After that you never have to think about it again.

Totem uses Android’s Accessibility Service to see which app you open in the foreground. That’s the only way Totem can recognise a blocked app and show the block screen. This happens entirely on your own device: nothing is stored and nothing is sent to us or to third parties.
On most devices the list jumps straight to Totem. If not, look under ‘Installed apps’ or ‘Downloaded apps’. Tap it and turn the switch on.

Is the switch greyed out, or does it switch off again right away? Then Android is blocking it because Totem didn’t come from the Play Store. Go to Settings → Apps → Totem → the three dots at the top right → ‘Allow restricted settings’, and try again.
This lets Totem show its block screen on top of the app you just opened.
Turn on the switch next to Totem.
Needed if you use schedules: this makes a block start on the minute instead of sometimes hours later.
Turn on ‘Allow setting alarms and reminders’.
Prevents your device from putting Totem to sleep and missing a schedule. Especially on Xiaomi, Oppo and Samsung this makes the difference.
Find Totem and choose ‘Don’t optimise’ or ‘Unrestricted’.
So you get a message when a schedule starts, and the timer stays visible during a block.
The app asks for this itself; open the app again and the prompt appears on its own.
You can always find this later under Settings.
Totem wants to use the Accessibility Service
Totem uses Android’s Accessibility Service (AccessibilityService). Below is what that means.
What Totem reads: as soon as you bring another app to the foreground, Totem gets a signal and reads only the name of that app.
What for: to check whether that app belongs to the focus mode you turned on and, if so, to show the block screen on top of it. Without this permission Totem can’t block anything.
What Totem doesn’t do: the content of your screen is not read, no keystrokes are stored and no screenshots are taken.
Data: the name of the opened app stays on this device. It is not stored, collected, shared or sold -- not to us and not to third parties.
You can always turn the service off later via Settings → Accessibility on your device, or via Settings in Totem.
If you tap \'I agree\', Totem takes you to the Android setting where you turn the service on yourself. If you tap \'Don’t agree\', nothing happens and the service stays off.
Needed to see which app you open. Without this Totem can’t block anything.

Needed to start a schedule on the minute. Without this a block can kick in hours late.
